title: perf(canary): auto-detect performance regressions and wire rollout guards
author: Asha Raman
description: Add an automatic regression detector for perf canaries and integrate rollout guards into the deployment pipeline. Motivation: reduce time-to-detect and automatically halt rollouts on statistically significant latency/throughput regressions observed by continuous canaries. This change implements a detector that runs after every canary batch, computes delta distributions against the baseline, applies adjustable thresholds and multiple-comparison corrections, and emits structured alerts that the rollout guard consumes. The rollout guard can pause or rollback canaries and optionally trigger an automatic model fallback or region reroute. Checklist: [x] core detector implementation; [x] rollout guard integration with deployment service; [x] telemetry + metrics + spans added; [x] unit + integration tests for detector logic; [x] console UI flags and docs updated; [x] Linear tasks linked. Related: ENG-2314, ENG-2891. Notes: default thresholds are conservative (p95 latency +10% and throughput -8% with p<0.01 after Bonferroni correction). Config is feature-flagged behind perf_canary.auto_detect and rollout_guards.enabled. Backwards compatible: if disabled, canaries run unchanged. This PR focuses on latency/throughput regression detection; quality/regression on output tokens will be separate work (ENG-3120).

release_notes: Add automatic detection of latency/throughput regressions for canaries (configurable thresholds)
Integrate rollout guards to pause/rollback deployments on significant regressions
Expose detector results via API and console UI flags
Feature-flagged and tuned to minimize false positives by default
review_comments: Jordan Lee: Nice work. Before approving, can you explain the choice of Bonferroni correction vs BH? I want to understand potential power loss when many metrics are monitored.

Asha Raman: We chose Bonferroni for now because the canary surface monitors a small, curated set of metrics for each rollout (latency p50/p95/p99, throughput, error-rate). BH is on the roadmap if we increase metric count (ENG-3125). Added a comment and config option to switch methods.

Priya Kapoor: Requesting stronger unit tests around low-sample scenarios and a fallback that doesn't pause rollouts too aggressively. Can you add an integration test where sample sizes are low and detector defers to a confidence floor?
Asha Raman: Added test_canary_rollout_guard.low_sample_size and introduced min_samples config (default 50). See perf-canary/tests/test_detector.py commit that stabilizes timing harness.
Marcus Holt: Verified telemetry spans and tagging for traceability. Approved after CI green and bench-compare rerun.
Jordan Lee: Approved. Rebase and squash before merge.
discussion_summary: The team agreed on conservative defaults to reduce false positives, feature-flagged rollout guards, and a follow-up to expand metric families and FDR control. Tests cover low-sample behavior and guard actions. Bench-compare initially flagged a minor regression; thresholds were tuned and the check passed on re-run.
notes_for_ops: Default thresholds are conservative; ops can tune via helm values perf_canary.detector.thresholds
When rollout_guard pauses a deployment, it emits a structured event to /events/canary/pause and posts a Slack alert to #canary-alerts by default
Make sure metric retention for canary baselines is at least 7 days for stable baselines
